title: phase24 double-free class: why per-site band-aids never converged and how the model fix closed it
content:
ROOT CAUSE: TML had no move semantics — every value-read of a refcounted payload (Shared/Sync/Heap.get, HashMap/List.get, iterator yields) was a BITWISE copy that aliased nested owned handles (Shared[U]/Heap[U] fields) without bumping their refcounts. The copy's drop-glue then decremented counts on storage the container still owned → nondeterministic double-free/UAF (heap-layout dependent, hence the phase24 "X/30 runs" crash lotteries).

WHY BAND-AIDS DIDN'T CONVERGE: the aliasing was manufactured by codegen at EVERY read site, so fixes were O(sites) and each per-site patch traded one failure mode for another: into_raw()/from_raw() chains suppressed the drop (= leak + fragile reconstruct ordering); deliberate leak fns (declarator_name_value_leak) leaked by design; manual .duplicate() at call sites created refcount bumps the consumer never released (phase24l: migrating ~40 sites REGRESSED the repro 29/30→25/30); making get require T: Duplicate hit generic-mono K001 codegen bugs (decision 009 alt (a)). Per-site fixes shift crash probability across heap layouts; they cannot remove the class.

HOW THE MODEL FIX CLOSED IT: structurally, at the two right layers. (1) codegen: ptr_read_clone[T] intrinsic (v0.3.52 + phase26b) — bitwise load + auto-emitted T::duplicate() for handle-bearing T, identity for primitives, transient temp never registered for drop — installed at every container read-out and in Sync/Heap.get; (2) library: F-013 direct-field refcount reads (no inner temp), try_unwrap null-after-move + weak-count guard, destroy releases elements; (3) compiler: move dataflow activated + drop flags (phase26f). phase26c (this task) then DELETED the remaining band-aids: Shared.get folded to ptr_read_clone (it was the last unsound bitwise reader), Shared.get_ref moved off the mis-typing ptr_as_ref intrinsic onto ref (*this.ptr).value, all hazard docstrings describing the dead class removed — and the determinism corpus (adversarial, poison+quarantine) stayed at floors, proving the FIX, not the workarounds, holds the tree up. The frozen compiler-tml/src/cc band-aid mass (180 .duplicate() calls, CollectedArgs, 10 manual impl Duplicate) remains for the self-hosting era (phases 30–33).

LESSON: when a bug class is manufactured by a compiler/codegen invariant violation, call-site mitigation is provably non-convergent — measure it (crash-rate corpus), fix the invariant, then delete every mitigation as the proof-of-fix.
